related_questions.question: How many people are waiting for asylum in the US?

text_blocks.snippet: As of January 31, 2025, there were over 3.7 million open removal cases in U.S. immigration courts, with 1,478,623 being defensive asylum applications, according to the American Immigration Council. This represents a significant backlog, with wait times for asylum cases often stretching for years.

list.title: Total Removal Cases:
list.snippet: Over 3.7 million cases were pending in immigration courts as of January 31, 2025, according to the American Immigration Council.

list.title: Asylum Applications:
list.snippet: Within those removal cases, 1,478,623 were specifically defensive asylum applications, meaning these individuals are defending against deportation and seeking asylum, according to the American Immigration Council.

list.title: Backlog Growth:
list.snippet: The number of pending asylum cases has been steadily increasing, with some estimates suggesting over 1.56 million people waiting for their asylum cases to be heard by late 2022.

list.title: Long Wait Times:
list.snippet: The backlog in the system translates to significant delays for asylum seekers, with some facing wait times of several years. For example, one source mentions an average wait time of approximately 4.3 years for claims in front of the Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR) and an estimated wait time of over 6 years for those before U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS).
